market_holds: Spot $2.13 at the 18:09 UTC seal ($2.19 intraday at 19:17 UTC), down 28.6% over 5 sessions and 42.8% over 20, at its 52-week low and 85% below the February 2026 high of about $14. The baseline's front-month straddle is 29.4% with 133.6% ATM IV, which nets to a 5.4% event move after ordinary volatility is removed; realised volatility is 128% annualised (about 8% a day) and the deadband is 8.1%. The run-in is mostly the tape: GDS fell 30.39 to 13.45 (-56%) from 2026-10-12 to 2026-11-20 while VNET fell 5.32 to 2.19 (-59%), 9698.HK fell in step, KWEB lost 16% from 11-06 and QQQ lost 17% from 746 to 617 (-4.3% on 11-20 alone). Each leg had a dated sector cause: a US bill against Chinese data-centre gear (around 10-02), Commerce closing the overseas Nvidia-leasing loophole, and worries about AI financing and Nvidia's leadership (VNET -9.6% on the day). I found no VNET-specific negative news in November. The only company items were a board seat for the CATL-linked holders (11-16) and a buyback of US$75.3m of the 2027 converts for about US$80m (10-27). Consensus for Q3 is about RMB3.00bn of revenue (Chartmill, cut 2.15% over three months), or about US$442m, +21.8% YoY in dollars (Earnings Whispers, 11-15). Full-year consensus of about US$1.74bn sits near the top of the reaffirmed RMB11.5-11.8bn guide (US$1.71-1.75bn), with adjusted EBITDA guided at RMB3.55-3.75bn and capex at RMB10-12bn. Bullish sentiment fell from 20.7% to 12.3%. Short interest is crowded but conflicting: 9-12 days to cover, about 48M shares per Chartmill on 10-15, borrow fee about 0.5%. Q2 (2026-08-18) gapped -11.6% and closed -16.9% after revenue came in narrowly light and the guide was only maintained, which shows the line it trades on is revenue against the guide and the wholesale move-in pace. Q3 2025 opened +5.8% and closed -1.2%.
view: The collapse is a sector and tape de-rating, not company news. The question is whether Monday's release confirms or contradicts what the tape has done. On the fundamental line, my arithmetic leans slightly negative. H1 2026 revenue was RMB5.47bn (Q1 2.69, Q2 2.78). A normal Q3 seasonal step (+6.2% QoQ, as Q2 to Q3 2025) gives about RMB2.95bn, roughly 1.7% under the RMB3.00bn consensus and +14% YoY, close to Q2's +14.2%. Even the guide's low end then needs about RMB3.08bn in Q4, and the top end, where consensus sits, needs about 3.38bn, which looks out of reach. Management only promised 'marginally faster' move-ins in H2 and tied them to domestic chip supply. Peer evidence splits by segment. Wholesale AI demand is strong: Runze's Q3 revenue rose 29.6% on a record 290MW delivered, and Tencent's Q3 capex rose about 527% to RMB81bn. Retail IDC is weak: Sinnet's IDC revenue grew 9% while gross margin fell 10pp on pricing pressure and slow move-ins, and Athub's revenue fell 2.3%. That is the mix that gave VNET a narrowly light Q2. So the most likely release is wholesale +25-30%, EBITDA on track, total revenue in line to slightly light, and the revenue guide kept or narrowed toward the low end. Against that, the price has fallen 59% in five weeks on no company news, 75% below the US$8.69/ADS the CATL-linked buyers paid (closed 2026-09-21, with a 'voting and consortium agreement' with the founder). It is a crowded short, and VNET was flat on 11-20 while GDS fell about 9% and QQQ 4%. A print that only shows the China AIDC demand is intact could bring a relief bid, and a guide trim on a levered equity (about US$620m market cap against about US$2.4bn net debt) could take another 15-20% off. Monday's tape, at the end of a violent AI-infrastructure rout, is likely to matter as much as the print inside a window that ends at 13:00 ET. I cannot separate these well enough to call a direction.

recommendation.reason: Arithmetic on the H2-weighted guide and weak retail-IDC peers points to Q3 revenue landing in line to slightly light and the FY revenue guide toward its low end, under a consensus near the top. That is the shape that drew -17% in August. But the stock has already lost 59% in five weeks on sector news, is a crowded short, and has a strategic holder in at four times the price, so a merely adequate print could just as well bring relief. Neither side reaches 65%, and Monday's market tape is a large unforecastable part of a window that ends at 13:00 ET.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: A Q3 revenue print at or above RMB3.0bn with the FY guide raised or reaffirmed at the top end, or a new large wholesale order or a CATL-backed funding or strategic plan in the release, would make the relief case dominant. A cut to the RMB11.5bn low end, with utilisation still falling, would make the downside case dominant.

self_critique: The strongest case against a slight down lean: the stock has fallen 67% since a print with the same narrowly-light shape, so that shape is now the bar, not a surprise. Wholesale peers and Chinese hyperscaler capex point to strong AI demand, and management may use the call for the 'fuller outlook' with big order and reservation numbers. A crowded short on a 59% sector-driven fall with a strategic holder far above makes a sharp relief bounce plausible even on an in-line print. Against an up lean: the equity is a thin slice of a levered capital structure in a market actively punishing AI financing, so a revenue trim is not cushioned. Both cases are real, and Monday's tape could swamp either. I stay near 50.
approach_notes: P6's decomposition of the run-in into peers and tape (GDS, KWEB, QQQ) was the most useful step, and P4's 'name what the move is tied to' kept me from reading the drawdown as a priced-in miss. Peer counterparties in Chinese-language sources were the freshest data. The window's exposure to Monday's market tape after a crash is a large component the playbook gives no tool for, beyond 'keep p_up about the release'.
